name: Dedication of the Basilica of Saint Mary Major
history: Soon after the Council of Ephesus proclaimed Mary the Mother of God in 431, Pope Sixtus III built a great basilica in her honour on the Esquiline Hill. It is among the oldest churches in the West dedicated to Our Lady and one of the four major basilicas of Rome. A later legend tells of snow falling there in August, so it is also called Our Lady of the Snows.
life: The basilica of Santa Maria Maggiore keeps much of its fifth-century form. The mosaics of Sixtus III still shine along the nave and over the triumphal arch, telling the story of the Old Testament and the childhood of Christ, and proclaiming the faith of Ephesus that Mary’s Son is truly God. A medieval legend says that in the time of Pope Liberius a Roman couple and the pope dreamed that Our Lady wished a church built where snow would fall, and on the morning of 5 August snow lay on the Esquiline. Each year white petals are let fall from the ceiling in memory of it. The basilica keeps the relic venerated as the wood of the crib of Bethlehem and the ancient icon of Our Lady called Salus Populi Romani. Several popes are buried there, among them Saint Pius V and, in 2025, Pope Francis.
prayerTo: Holy Mary, Mother of God, the people of Rome built a house for you when the Church first proclaimed your dignity. Make my heart a dwelling where your Son is welcome. Protect the Church, guard our families, and lead us to the house of the Father, where you wait for us. Amen.
penance: Pray the Rosary today, or one decade, for the Holy Father and for your own parish church.
meditation: The Church honours a building because of the One born of Mary. Where in your life have you made room for Christ, and where is there still no room at the inn?
prayer: Grant us, Your servants, O Lord God, we beseech You, to enjoy lasting health of mind and body; and by the intercession of glorious and blessed Mary, ever Virgin, may we be delivered from present sorrow and partake to the full of eternal happiness. Through our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
prayerSource: Collect of the day, Roman Missal of 1962
